newsitem.title: POLAND: Irena sees 1997 net up to PLN 9.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Irena sees 1997 net up to PLN 9.1 mln.

text.p: Polish glassmaker Irena SA expects to lift 1997 net profit to 9.1 million zlotys from a predicted flat 7.1-million-zloty net this year, the firm's president said on Wednesday.

Boleslaw Felczak told a news conference that Irena had invested virtually all the 19 million zlotys from its 1994 share issue, much going to the instalment of a new soda glass production line to become operative by June next year.
He said six million zlotys went in 1996 to a new crystal glass oven.
"The realisation of our development and our marketing strategy will allow us to make a net profit about 30 percent higher than in 1996," Felczak said, referring to 1997 earnings.

Felczak said the oven's start-up costs and a strengthening zloty were largely responsible for the firm's poor earnings in this year's first half, reflected in a third-quarter operating profit at two million zlotys against 0.8 million in the first.
Felczak told Reuters that the firm planned to invest another 15-18 million zlotys in 1997 and 1998, for which a new share or bond issue was possible.
He also said Irena, whose full name is Huta Szkla Gospodarczego Irena SA, was planning to buy stakes in firms in the glass industry.
The firm expects sales of 58 million zlotys this year and 80.5 million zlotys next year.
In the first 10 months this year the company netted 6.2 million zlotys on sales of 43.9 million zlotys.
